title: Kernel-first surjective comparison of cofactor maps
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $c,c'\geq0$, and let $E=[P\xrightarrow{u}Q]$, $E'=[P'\xrightarrow{u'}Q']$ be complexes in degrees $-1,0$ whose terms are finite projective $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], of ranks $c,c+1$ and $c',c'+1$ at every prime. Let $f=(f^{-1},f^0):E\to E'$ be a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so $f^0u=u'f^{-1}$. Put $C_E=Q/u(P)$, $D_E=(\bigwedge^cP)^\vee\otimes_A\bigwedge^{c+1}Q$, and likewise $C_{E'},D_{E'}$, with exterior powers [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra] and $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,A)$. Suppose given linear maps $w_E:C_E\to D_E$ and $w_{E'}:C_{E'}\to D_{E'}$ whose restrictions to every common finite standard free localization satisfy the cofactor formula
$$w_E(\bar v)=(p_1\wedge\cdots\wedge p_c)^\vee\otimes(u(p_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u(p_c)\wedge v),$$
and the analogous formula for $E'$, for any ordered source basis and any lift $v$.
Let $N^{-1}=\ker f^{-1}$, $N^0=\ker f^0$, and let $d_N:N^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}N^0$ and $T_f:D_E\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{E'}$ be the kernel differential and determinant comparison of [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus], expressed in dual-first order by ordinary tensor symmetry. On a common free localization choose a basis $k_1,\ldots,k_r$ of $N^{-1}$, put $l_i=d_N(k_i)$, choose bases $p'_1,\ldots,p'_{c'}$ and $q'_1,\ldots,q'_{c'+1}$, and choose linear sections of $f^{-1},f^0$ giving lifts $\widetilde p_j,\widetilde q_j$. Write $k,l,\widetilde p,\widetilde q,p',q'$ for their ordered wedges. These are kernel-first bases of $P,Q$, with $c=r+c'$ on each nonzero chart, and the comparison satisfies
$$T_f\bigl((k\wedge\widetilde p)^\vee\otimes(l\wedge\widetilde q)\bigr)=(p')^\vee\otimes q'.$$
For every $v\in Q$ one has
$$T_f(w_E(\bar v))=w_{E'}(\overline{f^0v}),\qquad T_f\circ w_E=w_{E'}\circ H^0(f).$$
The equation has sign $+1$ in this kernel-first convention, independently of all splittings and bases. It includes empty kernel and quotient source blocks, characteristic two and the zero ring; neither differential is required to be injective.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus], the kernel terms are finite projective and $d_N$ is an isomorphism. Projectivity of $P',Q'$ gives sections $s^{-1},s^0$ of the two surjections [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Thus $P=N^{-1}\oplus s^{-1}(P')$ and $Q=N^0\oplus s^0(Q')$: explicitly $x=(x-s^if^ix)+s^if^ix$, and the intersection is zero by applying $f^i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] to $N^{-1},P',Q'$. Products of their covering elements give a common finite standard cover, still generating the unit ideal (multiply the three expressions for $1$). On each chart choose $k,p',q'$ as in the statement; $l=d_N(k)$ is a basis of $N^0$, and the direct sums give the displayed kernel-first bases of $P,Q$. On a nonzero chart reduce these bases modulo any maximal ideal: their lengths give $c=r+c'$ and $c+1=r+c'+1$. Zero charts require no rank assertion.

proof.text: Write $e=(k\wedge\widetilde p)^\vee\otimes(l\wedge\widetilde q)$ and $e'=(p')^\vee\otimes q'$ on one chart. The exact-sequence maps of [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] send $k\otimes p'$ to $k\wedge\widetilde p$ and $l\otimes q'$ to $l\wedge\widetilde q$. The differential determinant is $\delta_N=k^\vee\otimes l$ in dual-first order. Therefore the definition of $\Gamma_f$ in [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus] gives $\Gamma_f(e'\otimes\delta_N)=e$, and its normalization gives $T_f(e)=e'$. These are computations of the localized global maps: [lem-trf-projective-exterior-scalar-comparisons] identifies the exterior powers, their duals, evaluation and tensor symmetry under scalar extension, and identifies the scalar-extended exact-sequence maps. The global splitting from Step 1 identifies the localized kernels with the kernels of the localized maps. The formula for $\delta_N$, and hence for $\Gamma_f$ and its inverse $T_f$, consequently localizes to the formula just calculated.

proof.text:
Work on this chart, with $v$ any element of $Q$ on the chart. Put $v'=f^0(v)$ and $x_j=u'(p'_j)$. The chain equation gives $u(\widetilde p_j)=s^0(x_j)+b_j$ with $b_j\in N^0$, and $v=s^0(v')+b$ with $b\in N^0$. Also $u(k_i)=l_i$. By multilinearity and alternation [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra],
$$u(k_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u(k_r)\wedge u(\widetilde p_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u(\widetilde p_{c'})\wedge v
=l\wedge s^0(x_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge s^0(x_{c'})\wedge s^0(v').$$
Indeed each discarded summand contains $l_1,\ldots,l_r$ and some $b_j$ or $b$; expand that vector in the basis $l_i$, so each term has a repeated factor and is zero. This uses $z\wedge z=0$, not division by $2$. No factor is permuted.

proof.text: There is a unique coefficient $a$ with $x_1\wedge\cdots\wedge x_{c'}\wedge v'=a q'$: this top exterior power is free with generator $q'$ by the determinant exact-sequence statement [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] (or its determinant-line definition). Applying the exterior power of the section $s^0$ and wedging $l$ gives the right hand side of Step 3 as $a(l\wedge\widetilde q)$. Thus the assumed cofactor formulas give $w_E(\bar v)=a e$ and $w_{E'}(\overline{v'})=a e'$. Step 2 and linearity imply $T_f(w_E(\bar v))=a e'=w_{E'}(\overline{f^0v})$. This proves the desired equation on every chart, including for arbitrary localized $v$; no injectivity of $u$ or $u'$ was used.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), kernel-first comparison construction preceding Tag 0FJJ; duality.tex Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), displayed cofactor formula. Agent-written compatibility calculation.

proof.text: For a global $v\in Q$, let $z=T_f(w_E(\bar v))-w_{E'}(\overline{f^0v})\in D_{E'}$. Its localization on every chart is zero by Steps 2--4 and the given local cofactor formulas. The injectivity clause of [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact] gives $z=0$. The chain equation makes $H^0(f):Q/u(P)\to Q'/u'(P')$, $\bar v\mapsto\overline{f^0v}$, well-defined; every cokernel element has a representative, so the elementwise equality is the equality of maps. The calculation works for every choice of sections and bases, while $T_f$ is the fixed normalized map of [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus], so the equation is independent of these choices. With $r=0$ all kernel wedges are $1$; with $c'=0$ the quotient source wedge is $1$ and Step 3 simply removes the kernel component of $v$. These formulas still have sign $+1$. Over the zero ring all modules and maps are zero and every asserted equality is unique. The alternation argument already covers characteristic two.
